title: Rebuild the stock front brake caliper
completeness: Complete stock front-caliper seal/piston service with removal, fluid replacement, bleeding and refit. Serviceable master cylinder, hose and disc required; damaged components need their own replacement operation.
entry_state: Assembled exact US2026 stock YZ450F; front wheel installed.
Original front master cylinder, hose and disc serviceable; correct replacement caliper seals and any needed pistons/pads available.
exit_state: Front caliper rebuilt and secured; hose connected, pads retained and reservoir closed.
Front circuit bled; leak, lever and brake-effect checks passed.

source.review_note: Visual139,140,141,145,146 and110 plus exact text closure. DiagramS means silicone grease; BF means brake fluid. No compressed-air pressure invented. Independent root review passed visual139/140/141/143–147/108–111; minimum-mark level clarification added before freeze.

applicability.included: Stock front brake on exact US2026 YZ450F
excluded: Damaged master cylinder/hose/disc requiring separate replacement

required_tools.name: Stable support, suitable hand tools and precision torque tools
Compressed-air supply, protective rag and eye protection
required_tools.size: For controlled piston extraction and clearing passages

required_tools.name: Clear bleed hose, waste container and clean fluid-safe trays

required_parts.name: Fresh DOT4 brake fluid
required_parts.purpose: Cleaning, lubrication and complete front-circuit refill

required_parts.name: Two piston seals and two dust seals
Silicone grease
required_parts.purpose: Only diagram-marked seals and sliding pins

required_parts.name: Replacement pistons and paired brake pads if inspection requires
required_parts.purpose: Match exact stock caliper; do not reuse failed parts

preflight: Use linked exploded views to identify seal grooves, pad springs and sliding pins.
Keep brake fluid away from eyes, painted surfaces and plastics; contain piston ejection with a rag.
critical_stop_conditions: Damaged bore/body/bracket or unserviceable replacement components.
Fluid leaks, persistent air, spongy lever or failed brake-effect check.

steps.title: Prepare the front circuit
steps.instruction: Secure the bike upright on level ground with reservoir top horizontal. Protect paint and plastic. Remove reservoir cap, diaphragm and float; keep parts clean.
steps.verification: Bike stable; only the front circuit is being opened.
steps.origin: Yamaha OEM service manual; original factual companion

steps.title: Drain and disconnect
steps.instruction: Remove caliper union bolt and both copper washers; put hose end in a catch container and pump out fluid. Discard drained fluid and washers.
steps.verification: Entire front circuit drained before caliper disassembly.
steps.origin: Yamaha OEM service manual; original factual companion

steps.title: Remove caliper and pads
steps.instruction: Remove pad-pin plug and loosen pin. Remove caliper mounting bolts, then pin, pads and both illustrated pad springs. Separate caliper and bracket; release hose holder if needed.
steps.verification: Keep spring positions matched to diagram139; wheel stays installed.
steps.origin: Yamaha OEM service manual; original factual companion

steps.title: Extract pistons
steps.instruction: Contain the pistons with a rag. Apply compressed air through the hose port to expel them; keep clear of their exit. Never pry pistons out. Remove both dust seals, both piston seals and bleed screw.
steps.verification: All four old seals removed; no piston or bore damage from extraction.
steps.origin: Yamaha OEM service manual; original factual companion

steps.title: Inspect the caliper
steps.instruction: Replace rusted, scratched or worn pistons. Replace the caliper for cylinder scratches/wear or body cracks/damage; replace a damaged bracket. Clear blocked fluid passages with compressed air.
steps.verification: Record findings; proceed only with serviceable or correctly replaced parts.
steps.origin: Yamaha OEM service manual; original factual companion

steps.title: Clean and renew seals
steps.instruction: Wash internal parts with fresh DOT4, never solvent. Install two new piston seals and two new dust seals in their respective diagram140 grooves; use silicone grease at its S-marked seal positions.
steps.verification: Correct new seals fully seated; piston seal inward of dust seal as illustrated.
steps.origin: Yamaha OEM service manual; original factual companion

steps.title: Reassemble pistons and bracket
steps.instruction: Lubricate pistons with fresh DOT4 and install as diagram140. Apply silicone grease at diagram139 sliding-pin locations and reunite bracket/caliper. Install bleed screw at5 Nm.
steps.verification: Pistons seated without seal damage; sliding assembly moves correctly.
steps.origin: Yamaha OEM service manual; original factual companion

steps.title: Reconnect the hose
steps.instruction: Position bracket/caliper temporarily. Fit hose with two new copper washers; its pipe portion must contact the caliper stop. Tighten union bolt to30 Nm.
steps.verification: Record new washers, stop contact and30 Nm union torque.
steps.origin: Yamaha OEM service manual; original factual companion

steps.title: Restore pads and mounting
steps.instruction: Check lining thickness: replace pads as a set at the1.0 mm wear limit. Restore both pad springs to diagram139, engage pad projections in caliper recesses and fit pin temporarily. Secure caliper mounting bolts28 Nm, pin17 Nm and plug2.5 Nm.
steps.verification: Record lining assessment and mounting/pin/plug torques; pads correctly retained.
steps.origin: Yamaha OEM service manual; original factual companion

steps.title: Secure hose routing
steps.instruction: If released, align hose-holder upper edge with the hose paint mark and tighten holder bolt9 Nm. Confirm original routing without strain.
steps.verification: Holder secured and hose routed as illustrated.
steps.origin: Yamaha OEM service manual; original factual companion

steps.title: Fill for bleeding
steps.instruction: Fill reservoir above the minimum mark shown on PDF109 with fresh DOT4 and fit diaphragm. Attach a secure clear hose to bleeder, with its free end in a catch container. Keep reservoir supplied throughout; prevent water entry and overflow.
steps.verification: Reservoir horizontal; correct fluid and sufficient supply.
steps.origin: Yamaha OEM service manual; original factual companion

steps.title: Remove trapped air
steps.instruction: Slowly pump lever several times, then pull fully and hold. Open bleeder; close it before releasing lever. Repeat until hose fluid contains no bubbles, replenishing reservoir. If stubborn tiny bubbles persist, let fluid settle a few hours and repeat.
steps.verification: Record bubble-free result; never allow reservoir to empty.
steps.origin: Yamaha OEM service manual; original factual companion

steps.title: Close the circuit
steps.instruction: Tighten bleeder5 Nm and refit its cap. Restore fluid above the minimum mark shown on PDF109 with bike upright and reservoir horizontal. Refit float, diaphragm and cap in diagram141 order; cap screws1.5 Nm. Clean spills immediately.
steps.verification: Record final level, bleeder and cap torque; all openings closed.
steps.origin: Yamaha OEM service manual; original factual companion

steps.title: Verify brake function
steps.instruction: Apply front brake repeatedly and inspect hose/connections for leaks. Lever must not feel soft or spongy; bleed again if it does. After stationary checks pass, check brake effect on a dry test surface before normal riding.
steps.verification: Record no leaks, firm lever and proper braking; unresolved faults prevent completion.
steps.origin: Yamaha OEM service manual; original factual companion
